lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary on a U.S.-style résumé and disclose personal information employers do not need at this stage.

items.says: Confirm the contact URL is a real, working profile rather than a placeholder.
items.because: A broken or generic link can undermine the application.

items.says: Put Stonebridge before Crescent.
items.because: Experience should normally be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Standardize currency and number formatting throughout.
items.because: Consistent formatting makes the figures easier to scan.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not ordinarily hedge the stated holdings.
items.because: It would ordinarily add fixed-rate exposure rather than hedge existing holdings.

items.says: Add the size of the declined-application sample.
items.because: It would make the approval-rate change more credible.

items.says: Give the period over which early defaults were observed.
items.because: It would make the “no rise” claim more credible.

items.says: Change “Writes” to a tense appropriate for a role that ended in 2022.
items.because: The current tense does not match the ended role.

items.says: Clarify the period covered by the reduction in missed covenant tests.
Clarify what kind of time fell from 6 hours to 3.
items.because: It is unclear whether the figure means analyst hours, elapsed time, or another measure.

items.says: Specify the forecast-error measure.
items.because: The claim that error stayed under 4% needs a defined measure.

items.says: Specify the period over which forecast error stayed below 4%.
Clarify what the USD 600M describes.
items.because: The company’s scale is otherwise ambiguous.

items.says: Substantiate the link between the forecast and early debt repayment.
items.because: The repayment result should be retained only if that link can be substantiated.

items.says: Add evidence that the faster close maintained accuracy or controls, if available.
items.because: Automation alone can raise that question.

items.says: Confirm the scope of “every request.”
items.because: That wording is broad.

items.says: Add evidence of how the capital-plan template was adopted or used, if available.
Fix the opening gerund’s tense.
items.because: The bullet describes completed work but starts with “Mapping.”

items.says: Restructure the sentence.
items.because: Its action and result are difficult to follow.

items.says: Clarify the period covered by the reduction in manual journal entries.
Explain how the before-and-after journal-entry figures were measured.
The FCFE cash-flow measure and WACC discount rate are inconsistent.
items.because: FCFE is normally discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is normally used with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: Say whether the controllers adopted the template or how widely it was used, if known.
items.because: That would make the outcome more tangible.

items.says: Clarify which valuation result was within 6% of the market price.
Give the date used for the market-price comparison.
Explain the purpose of the market-price comparison.
items.because: A market-price match by itself does not establish model quality.

items.says: The stated 25% drop is incorrect; a fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20%.
Clarify whether “1 point” means one percentage point of discount rate.
Define how forecast accuracy was measured.
Explain what the 10-year period represents.
Calling the move from 70% to 82% a 12% increase is incorrect.
items.because: It is a 12-percentage-point increase, not a 12% relative increase.

items.says: Explain how the accuracy change was validated.
items.because: A long-range forecast cannot be assessed without a stated comparison or backtest.

items.says: Check whether “FP&A team” accurately describes the team and work.
items.because: In a student investment fund, it may sound unrelated or imprecise.

items.says: Specify the analysis or reporting performed.
items.because: The current bullet is generic.

items.says: Specify the timeframe or decision the performance report supported.
items.because: The bullet relies only on committee use.

items.says: Show how the onboarding notes were used or whom they helped, if supportable.
items.because: Their impact is not shown.

items.says: Add other relevant software, systems, or analytical tools you can genuinely use.
items.because: Listing only Excel is very limited for a finance résumé.

items.says: Specify relevant Excel capabilities.
items.because: They may be important to the target roles.

items.says: Make sure each listed method is supported by an experience or project bullet.
items.because: The methods listed are broad.
